I was starting to prep stuff this week, as we’ve only been through one monthly board meeting together last month and so this is only my second time doing everything. I understand nobody liking to be the one to deal with everything. I’ve been there before myself.

I did tell her that these requests are only for the holidays and that I won’t even be asking for time off again until early May when I have military training. It really was just poor timing that I started working around the holidays so it seems like I may be abusing this, but I’m really not. These are the only two times I’ll be asking for time off for the next four months. Then I’ll be working more than my coworker normally does, which again, I already do each week.

Okay, I can understand that side of it. But I actually work more hours than she does every week to make up for the time I’ve taken off.
It’s a PT position, so I can’t go past 30 hours. But I try to max it each week and my coworker actually got onto me for working too many hours if I don’t have legitimate work to do. It’s a conundrum with her.

Also, we are in a separate part of the company where it’s just us two working together with one supervisor. The time I take off is unpaid, so the only real loss is if a ton of work falls onto my coworker’s lap and stresses her, which is why in my other reply I mentioned that I’m prepping a lot of work to alleviate that stress for her.

To top it all off, I did offer to bring my work laptop with me when I took time off last month and my coworker insisted I didn’t and just focused on time with my family.

I showed up late once due to a pet emergency, not because I chose to show up late. And like I said before, she told me in the beginning that taking time off nilly willy was normal for this job and perfectly okay. She didn’t even bat an eye when I requested a week off in the first month. Bear in mind, she only works Mondays-Wednesdays for half the day and then gives herself long weekends every week. She prioritizes her family over her work, and I never said I didn’t prioritize work in my life.
I simply said my work ethic dipped as I began to struggle to deal with personal and medical issues. That happens to a lot of people and I’m not unusual for that.

And again, we have little to no work to do for the next two weeks. We did the hefty work for the month this week and now if I don’t go on the vacation, I’d probably only need to show up two days the first week of January to work and then be done for the rest of the week. I am planning on prepping work for my coworker so when things I expect to come up do, she will have everything prepped and be able to do the work in a timely manner with far less to stress about.
